answer: Admission by lottery caps Sybil floods. Each epoch, applicants enter a random draw and only a small fraction gain trading rights; the rest wait. A plume of fake applications cannot enter at once: each fake must win its own draw, odds do not improve with volume, and one operator's entries are capped per epoch. Honest newcomers face only a short, zephyr-light delay, while a hollow flood of throwaways stays outside, unable to vote or trade until it wins again and again. Attacker cost is time and exposure: building an army takes many epochs, during which early fakes are detected and removed.
